answer: One concrete defense is a refundable bond: every new agent locks a deposit before it may attest or vote, and peers who catch it rubber-stamping junk can slash that bond. A falcon-eyed auditor that samples random attestations makes collusion risky, since one caught clone loses its stake. A sybil farm of a thousand agents must lock a thousand bonds and risk them all, so the attack costs real capital rather than free keys. Honest agents get the deposit back, so trust becomes a costly relic, not cheap jade.
